claims: Ruth's Chris Steak House maintains a business casual to elegant dress code for its dining rooms.
Specific requirements may vary slightly by location at Ruth's Chris Steak House.
All guests are asked to remove hats when entering the dining rooms of Ruth's Chris Steak House.
Guests wearing ball caps may be directed to dine in the bar or lounge areas instead.
Athletic and gym wear including workout gear, sweatpants, and yoga pants is generally not permitted in the main dining rooms of Ruth's Chris Steak House.
Tank tops, sleeveless shirts for men, and overly revealing outfits are prohibited in the main dining rooms of Ruth's Chris Steak House.
Undergarments should not be visible in the main dining rooms of Ruth's Chris Steak House.
Clothing with offensive language or graphics is not allowed in the main dining rooms of Ruth's Chris Steak House.
Swimwear and typical pool-related clothing are restricted in the main dining rooms of Ruth's Chris Steak House.
Cut-off shorts are barred in the main dining rooms of Ruth's Chris Steak House.
Clothing emitting a strong marijuana odor is barred in the main dining rooms of Ruth's Chris Steak House.
The dress code is generally more relaxed in the bar, lounge, and outdoor patio areas of Ruth's Chris Steak House.
Team support jerseys and hats are typically welcome in the bar, lounge, and outdoor patio areas of Ruth's Chris Steak House even when restricted in the main dining room.
Hats and headgear are prohibited in the dining rooms of Ruth's Chris Steak House.
Hats and headgear are allowed in the bar and patio areas of Ruth's Chris Steak House.
Gym wear, sweatpants, and tank tops are not permitted in the dining rooms of Ruth's Chris Steak House
